summary: Careful, preregistered paired study measuring verifier impact on synthetic intent→configuration tasks. Execution and analysis are complete and well-archived. Result: baseline 499/500 pass, guarded 500/500 pass; absolute improvement 0.002 (95% CI [0.0,0.006]); McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Methods, preregistration, and artifact bundle are present. Manuscript is scientifically defensible but requires a small set of clarifications to avoid reader confusion about shared-generation semantics, model-call accounting, and verifier scope/repair activity.
critical_issues: Methods do not explicitly state that baseline and guarded used a single shared initial LLM generation per task (shared_initial_candidate), which explains why only ~501 model calls were used instead of two independent calls per arm. Absent this clarification, readers may misinterpret the paired design and model-call accounting.

The manuscript omits a concise, explicit summary of verifier modeling scope and repair activity (e.g., which device/feature classes were modeled, count of excluded tasks—zero—and that only one repair invocation occurred). This gap can mislead readers about generalizability and the practical meaning of the guarded arm.

The statistical reporting (exact McNemar p = 1.00) is presented without brief explanation of why the p-value is 1.00 in the presence of a single discordant pair and without an explicit statement that the analysis is underpowered to detect small improvements because of a ceiling effect. This risks reader confusion about test interpretation.
required_revisions: In Methods (and Disclosure if appropriate) add an explicit, brief statement that generation_semantics was 'shared_initial_candidate' with independent_condition_generation = false, so each task used one shared LLM proposal (one generation call) that was then evaluated for both baseline and guarded conditions; add this same accounting to the Execution/Results paragraph and reconcile it with the reported model_calls_used = 501 and stage_counts (shared_initial_generation = 500, repair = 1). Use the archived execution manifest hashes as provenance but do not paste raw logs in body.

Add a short, explicit paragraph (or a row in Results/Limitations) listing the deterministic validator's modeled feature scope and confirm that zero tasks were excluded from the primary analysis; state the total number of repair invocations (1) and how that was counted (referencing the 'repair' stage count in the execution manifest). This must be derived from the supplied execution/analysis artifacts.

In Results add one clarifying sentence explaining the exact-McNemar p = 1.00 outcome (i.e., only one discordant pair observed, n10=1 n01=0, resulting in a two-sided exact test p=1.00) and explicitly state that the near-ceiling baseline pass rate substantially limits power to detect small absolute improvements (so the null result should be read as a ceiling-effect finding rather than evidence that verifiers are universally unnecessary).
optional_revisions: Include a one-paragraph per-cluster (VLAN/ACL/static-route) success-rate breakdown and the paired contingency figure (paired_difference_figure.svg) from the archived analysis artifacts to help readers judge heterogeneity; these artifacts are available in the evidence bundle.

Move or summarize a single-line provenance pointer in Methods to the representative artifact hashes (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl) to help reviewers locate archived logs quickly (do not paste full logs).

Add a very brief note in Discussion contrasting shared-initial-generation design choice with an alternative independent-generation design and state how that choice affects the estimand interpretation (i.e., guarded effect isolates verifier+repair impact conditional on the same initial model candidate).
